 Coram: Honourable Justice Smt. G. Anupama
 Chakravarthy
Oral Order
1. The aforesaid Interlocutory Application has been filed by the appellant seeking suspension of his sentence during pendency of the appeal.

2. The appellant stood convicted for the offences under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012, Sections 363/34, 323 and 341 of the Indian Penal Code vide judgment dated 29.10.2021 passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Court, Supaul passed in POCSO Case No. 52/2019 arising out of Nirmali P.S. Case 166/2019 corresponding to Tr. No. 81/2021.

Vide order dated 03.11.2021, the appellant has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 10 years, to pay a fine of Rs.
One Lakh and Fifty Thousand Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.390 of 2022(7) dt.24-12-2025 and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 03 years for the offence under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012, to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 07 years, to pay a fine of Rs. Fifty Thousand and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 01 year and 06 months for the offence under Section 363/34 IPC, to undergo simple imprisonment for 01 year, to pay a fine of Rs. One Thousand and in default of payment of fine to undergo simple imprisonment for 03 months for the offence under Section 323 IPC and to undergo simple imprisonment for 01 month along with a fine of Rs. Five Hundred and in default of payment of fine,
to suffer simple imprisonment for 07 days for the offence under Section 341 IPC.
All the sentences were directed to run concurrently.

sentences.text: Initially, a case vide Nirmali P.S. Case No. 166/2019 was registered on 06.10.2019 for the offences under Sections 376/34, 341, 323, 363 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 on the fardbeyan of the mother of victim (PW6) stating therein that on 05.10.2019 at about 5 P.M., the victim/daughter of the informant aged about 14 years along with one of her friends, had gone to Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.390 of 2022(7) dt.24-12-2025 view a fair at Nirmali but they did not return till 11 P.M. and on search they were found at Laukahi Police Station.

The victim disclosed that while she was returning with her friend from the fair about 9 P.M., they were intercepted by two boys on motorcycle, who took both of them in an orchard at Jarauli and started teasing them, whereafter two other boys also came there on motorcyle and started beating those boys, upon which, they fled away.

However, two boys who subsequently came there committed rape with both the girls and on protest they also assaulted the victim and another girl but having seen the police, they fled away from the place of occurrence.
4. After submission of chargesheet and after framing of charges, the Trial begun and in the trial, the appellant was found guilty and was convicted in the manner aforesaid.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that none of the independent witnesses have supported the case of prosecution and further, the Doctor (PW7), who examined the victim, had found no sign of sexual assault on the victim.

Apart from that, it has also been submitted that the witnesses examined on behalf of the prosecution are either Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.390 of 2022(7) dt.24-12-2025 family members or hearsay witnesses and, therefore, the appellant has a better chance to succeed herein in this appeal.
6.

The main contention of the Learned Counsel for the appellant for suspension of sentence of the appellant during the pendency of the appeal is that the maximum sentence awarded to the appellant is 10 years and the appellant has been languishing in jail since 17.10.2019 and has completed more than half of the sentence.

7. It appears that while the Interlocutory Application 01/2025 was still pending, another Interlocutory Application vide I.A. No. 02/2025 has also been filed by the appellant for grant of provisional bail during the pendency of the appeal on the ground that he has to attend Shradh Karma of his father, who died on 21.12.2025.

8. Since, the Interlocutory Application No. 01/2025, which was filed for suspension of sentence during the pendency of appeal is still pending, this Court deems it fit and proper to dispose off both the Interlocutory Applications by this common order.

9. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case as also taking into Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.390 of 2022(7) dt.24-12-2025 consideration the period of custody of the appellant since 07.10.2019, this Court is inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant during the pendency of the appeal.

10. Let, the appellant /Rohit Kumar be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his furnishing bonds in the sum of Rs. 10,000 (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount Rohit Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156432334/
2 each to the satisfaction of the Learned Special Judge, POCSO Court, Supaul in connection with POCSO Case No. 52/2019 arising out of Nirmali P.S. Case 166/2019 corresponding to Tr. No.
81/2021.
11.
